title: Localization of one supplied integral scalar mate
statement: Fix a prime $l$, an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_l$, schemes $X,Y$, finite coefficient stages $E,L$, and a $\mathbf Q_l$-algebra embedding $i:E\to L$. Let $A,B$ be exact integral Operations at $E,L$ [def-sf-constructible-exceptional-coefficient-construction-data], with both functors linear over their integral coefficient rings. Assume the integral constructible and finite-Tor predicates agree at both endpoints and both coefficient fields. Let $R,S$ be exact adjunction structures on their explicit raw rational tensor functors [lem-sf-integral-adjunction-raw-localization]. Suppose qA and qB are counit-normalized localization comparisons whose left and right components on every integral representative are identity. Let SX and SY be integral Scalar functors along the completed coefficient change for i. Assume that after ambient full inclusion these are literally the published integralScalarExtensionOfUniverses functors. Given a counit-normalized comparison d between A and B along SX,SY, there exists a counit-normalized rational comparison between the two fixed rational Operations, along the published rationalScalar functors. For every integral X-object K its left component at the raw rationalization of K is heterogeneously equal to rationalization at L of d.q.hom.app K. The heterogeneous equality transports only the underlying equal represented objects. This statement involves one coefficient embedding, with no compactification, compact-support realization, or identity/composition cocycle. Both endpoint scalar shift structures are prescribed by requiring their identity-normalized scalar localization comparison squares to commute with every integer shift, retaining the canonical endpoint rationalization shift comparisons in the squares. The supplied localization comparisons use the fixed canonical integralRationalizationShift on both endpoints.

proof.text: Use the published rational scalar object and pure-tensor map formulas at coefficient one. The supplied equality after the ambient full inclusion identifies the integral scalar object and map. Full-subcategory extensionality and proof irrelevance give literal functor equalities Q_E T = S Q_L on both endpoints.

The full integral representative functor is an equivalence when the supplied constructible and finite-Tor predicates agree. Transport the known categorical localization property of the raw tensor localization along this equivalence. Thus precomposition by rationalization is fully faithful. Descend the natural isomorphisms obtained by pasting qA inverse, the scalar localization equality, the given d, qB and the inverse endpoint equality, and do the same for b. The map-preimage equation gives their integral component formulas.

Use the canonical endpoint rationalization shifts and commShiftOfLocalization to put shifts on each rational scalar functor. Its canonical identity-normalized localization isomorphism commutes with every integer shift by the localization shift theorem. Pasting exact natural isomorphisms makes the two integral pasted comparisons commute with shifts. Cancel precomposition by rationalization in each shift equation; its shift comparison is invertible, so the descended q and b commute with every shift.

Identity-normalized qA and qB identify the rational counits at integral objects with the localized integral counits. Substitute the descended component formulas into the rational counit square. Cancel the adjacent endpoint comparison inverses, apply naturality of the target counit, use naturality of the identity-normalized qB to commute the target operation with rationalization on the integral b component, and apply localization to d.counit. Naturality of the scalar localization comparison closes the square. Every rational object is an integral representative by the supplied predicate equality. This also works in zero categories and for identity embeddings.

Package the descended isomorphisms, their counit equation and the descended shift equations as a CounitFieldComparison. The equality-comparison transports disappear heterogeneously in the component equation, leaving exactly Q_L(d.q). Both endpoint scalarShiftLocalization conclusions are the previously constructed canonical localization squares with their full integer-shift compatibility.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_integral_scalar_mate_localization
    (E L : FieldStage.{max u v} l) (i : E.carrier →ₐ[Padic l] L.carrier)
    (A : Operation.{u, v} l Ω X Y (.integral E))
    (B : Operation.{u, v} l Ω X Y (.integral L))
    [A.F.Additive] [A.G.Additive] [B.F.Additive] [B.G.Additive]
    [A.F.Linear (Padic.coefficientExtensionIntegers l E.carrier)]
    [A.G.Linear (Padic.coefficientExtensionIntegers l E.carrier)]
    [B.F.Linear (Padic.coefficientExtensionIntegers l L.carrier)]
    [B.G.Linear (Padic.coefficientExtensionIntegers l L.carrier)]
    {hEX : sfIntegralConstructible l E.carrier X = finiteTorConstructibleIntegral l E.carrier X}
    {hEY : sfIntegralConstructible l E.carrier Y = finiteTorConstructibleIntegral l E.carrier Y}
    {hLX : sfIntegralConstructible l L.carrier X = finiteTorConstructibleIntegral l L.carrier X}
    {hLY : sfIntegralConstructible l L.carrier Y = finiteTorConstructibleIntegral l L.carrier Y}
    (R : RawLocalizedAdjunction.{u, v} l Ω E X Y A hEX hEY)
    (S : RawLocalizedAdjunction.{u, v} l Ω L X Y B hLX hLY)
    (qA : CounitFieldComparison.{u, v} l Ω A (R.operation l Ω E)
      (rationalization.{u, v} l Ω E X) (rationalization.{u, v} l Ω E Y))
    (qB : CounitFieldComparison.{u, v} l Ω B (S.operation l Ω L)
      (rationalization.{u, v} l Ω L X) (rationalization.{u, v} l Ω L Y))
    (hqA : ∀ K, HEq (qA.q.hom.app K)
      (𝟙 ((rationalization.{u, v} l Ω E Y).obj (A.F.obj K))))
    (hbA : ∀ M, HEq (qA.b.hom.app M)
      (𝟙 ((rationalization.{u, v} l Ω E X).obj (A.G.obj M))))
    (hqB : ∀ K, HEq (qB.q.hom.app K)
      (𝟙 ((rationalization.{u, v} l Ω L Y).obj (B.F.obj K))))
    (hbB : ∀ M, HEq (qB.b.hom.app M)
      (𝟙 ((rationalization.{u, v} l Ω L X).obj (B.G.obj M))))
    (hsAX : qA.shiftX = integralRationalizationShift.{u, v} l Ω E X)
    (hsAY : qA.shiftY = integralRationalizationShift.{u, v} l Ω E Y)
    (hsBX : qB.shiftX = integralRationalizationShift.{u, v} l Ω L X)
    (hsBY : qB.shiftY = integralRationalizationShift.{u, v} l Ω L Y)
    (SX : Scalar.{u, v} l Ω (s := .integral E) (t := .integral L)
      (PurCompactSupport.completedChange l E.carrier L.carrier i) X)
    (SY : Scalar.{u, v} l Ω (s := .integral E) (t := .integral L)
      (PurCompactSupport.completedChange l E.carrier L.carrier i) Y)
    (hSX : SX.functor ⋙ RingStage.inclusion.{u, v} l Ω X (.integral L) =
      RingStage.inclusion.{u, v} l Ω X (.integral E) ⋙
        integralScalarExtensionOfUniverses l E.carrier L.carrier i X)
    (hSY : SY.functor ⋙ RingStage.inclusion.{u, v} l Ω Y (.integral L) =
      RingStage.inclusion.{u, v} l Ω Y (.integral E) ⋙
        integralScalarExtensionOfUniverses l E.carrier L.carrier i Y)
    (d : letI := SX.commShift
      letI := SY.commShift
      CounitComparison.{u, v} l Ω A B SX.functor SY.functor) :
    letI := SX.commShift
    letI := SY.commShift
    ∃ e : CounitFieldComparison.{u, v} l Ω (R.operation l Ω E) (S.operation l Ω L)
        (rationalScalar.{u, v} l Ω E L i X) (rationalScalar.{u, v} l Ω E L i Y),
      (∀ K : C.{u, v} l Ω X (.integral E),
        HEq (e.q.hom.app ((rationalization.{u, v} l Ω E X).obj K))
          ((rationalization.{u, v} l Ω L Y).map (d.q.hom.app K))) ∧
      scalarShiftLocalization.{u, v} l Ω E L i X SX e.shiftX ∧
      scalarShiftLocalization.{u, v} l Ω E L i Y SY e.shiftY

statement_change.what: The old scalarShiftLocalization compared raw shift components by HEq for every integer. The chosen rational triangulation API only fixes the literal tensor shift and identity localization component at one. A coherent shift can have other shift functors replaced by naturally isomorphic functors with different objects; literal HEq does not express invariance under that choice. Replace this extra strictness by the actual all-integer exactness square of the identity-normalized scalar localization comparison, with the fixed endpoint rationalization shifts. The original theorem signature, its q normalization, and the counit and shift conditions on its comparison are unchanged.

old_proof.text: Apply the ambient scalar equalities on objects and arrows. Fullness of the integral inclusions and proof irrelevance identify the given scalar maps with the completed scalar maps on the full integral categories.

Localize the components of the given q and b with the target localization functor. The published rational scalar functor has the semilinear tensor formula. Its coefficient map sends the source uniformizer to a unit in the target localization. The semilinear extension and transformation theorems extend the integral naturality and inverse equations to every tensor arrow, so these components form natural isomorphisms.

The identity q and b components of qA and qB identify the rational counits with the localized integral counits. Substitution in the proposed rational counit square reduces it to the target localization applied to d.counit. Functoriality gives the required equation. Every rational object has its integral representative by the supplied predicate equalities.

Extend the endpoint scalar shifts by the same semilinear construction. Localize d.qShift and d.bShift and use exact comparison localization to obtain the shift equations. The component formula of the construction gives the required normalization, including identity embeddings and zero Hom modules. The scalar endpoint shifts are normalized on every integral representative and every integer by localization of the given scalar shifts, which determines these structures uniquely.
